To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crisis was caused by the failure of corporate governance in the financial sector, and the root cause was the combination of strong incentives, low controls, flawed accounting, low quality and/or integrity of human capital, and a corrosive culture.

the financial crisis was the result of a lethal combination of strong incentives, poor risk management and controls, weak accounting and flawed internal and external reporting, inadequate human capital, and a corrosive culture.
the crisis was caused by five systems: incentives, risk management and control, accounting, human capital, and culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how organizations are governed and how they can be improved.
understanding the causes and consequences of the financial crisis, and with developing a new model of corporate governance that will help us avoid future crises.
the design of governance structures to mitigate agency problems in the context of a firm s competitive environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the root cause was that the incentives were too strong, the controls too weak, the accounting flawed, the people not skilled enough or of low integrity, and the culture corrosive.

the crisis was caused by a combination of incentives, control, accounting, human capital, and culture, which together produced a systemically risky firm, and that the solution is a comprehensive and detailed improvement program.
the root causes of the crisis can only be understood by looking at the five systems and how they interact.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the financial crisis of 2010 was a result of a failure of corporate governance.
we have met the enemy and he is us.
the financial crisis of 2018 was the product of a failure of corporate governance, and that we need to rethink the way we manage our systemically important firms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem is not just the system, but the people in the system.
the problem of governance is not primarily one of regulation. It is one of management.
the problem is not just a failure of regulators or a failure of the system.
